hero.headline: Judge reopens Trump IRS lawsuit to review $1.8 billion settlement
hero.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, agreeing to examine a $1.8 billion settlement that the Trump administration reached with the Justice Department. The settlement established what Trump has termed an "anti-weaponization" fund.

Judge Kathleen Williams reopened the case after receiving a motion from a third party arguing that the settlement "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court." The lawsuit was originally brought by Trump and his sons following the leak of their personal and business tax returns by a former contractor.

The Trump administration has characterized the settlement as compensation for what it describes as improper government targeting. The fund's stated purpose is to address instances of what Trump calls weaponization of government agencies.

The settlement has generated significant opposition and controversy since its announcement earlier this month. The backlash has exposed divisions within the Republican Party, with some party members publicly questioning whether the agreement serves the public interest and whether the legal basis for such a large settlement is sound.

The judge's decision to reopen the case and examine whether the settlement constitutes fraud suggests judicial concern about the terms of the agreement. Legal observers note that judicial review of executive branch settlements, while not routine, can occur when questions arise about the propriety of such arrangements.

Trump originally filed the lawsuit as part of a broader dispute with the IRS over tax matters. The Justice Department then negotiated and reached the $1.8 billion settlement with the administration, which established the controversial fund.

The reopening of the case means active litigation will resume as the judge examines the circumstances and details surrounding the settlement agreement. The judge has ordered Trump to address what court filings describe as serious allegations in the case.

The settlement has lacked substantial detail in its public disclosures, which has contributed to concerns raised by critics and the third-party motion filed with the court. These gaps in transparency have fueled questions about how the fund will be administered and whether it constitutes an appropriate use of government resources.

The case now returns to active litigation status. However, no timeline has been announced for how long the judge's review will take or when she might issue a ruling on the fraud allegations and other matters under examination.

The situation reflects broader tensions within the Republican Party regarding executive power, government spending, and the administration's legal strategy. The dispute over the settlement's propriety has divided party members on whether such an agreement represents sound governance or an inappropriate use of taxpayer funds.

cards.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
cards.body:
U.S. Central Command announced on Saturday that it prevented another vessel from docking at an Iranian port as part of its ongoing naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The military disabled a ship flying under a Gambian flag on Friday after the vessel ignored repeated warnings, according to a Centcom statement. The action represents the latest enforcement of restrictions the U.S. has placed on Iranian ports and the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical shipping channel for global oil supplies. The U.S. blockade reflects the strategic importance of the waterway to international commerce and energy markets.

Centcom did not provide specific details about the extent of damage to the disabled vessel or information about the condition of its crew. The military statement only confirmed that the ship failed to comply with warnings before U.S. forces took action.

The incident occurs amid a broader confrontation in the region with multiple environmental consequences. The U.S. has sunk several Iranian vessels at the start of military operations, while Iran has used drones and missiles to strike container ships and oil tankers in an effort to police its own blockade of the strait.

One significant casualty has been the Shahid Bagheri, an Iranian Navy vessel described as a converted container ship equipped with a short runway for launching drones. The ship was struck by U.S. warplanes on March 6 and subsequently grounded in shallow waters in the Khuran strait. The vessel has been leaking heavy fuel oil in Iranian territorial waters, creating an environmental hazard.

Satellite analysis indicates the oil slick has traveled westward toward the Hara biosphere reserve, the largest mangrove forest on the Gulf shoreline. As of March 18, the oil had moved approximately 16 miles southwest toward the ecologically sensitive area. Rainfall on March 27 appeared to accelerate the spill's movement further.

The potential impact on the Hara region could be significant. The area serves as critical habitat for migrating birds, critically endangered turtles, and numerous species of fish and crustaceans. Coastal fishing communities in the region depend almost entirely on the sea for their livelihoods.

The environmental damage extends beyond this single spill. Multiple incidents have occurred in the Gulf, including three small spills off the coasts of Iraq and Kuwait and another in the strait from a sunken container ship. A U.S. torpedo attack on the Iranian navy ship Dena off Sri Lanka also caused a spill that was handled by Sri Lankan authorities.

Environmental analysts warn the situation could deteriorate. With ongoing military strikes targeting ships in the region, the risk of more significant environmental disasters remains high.

cards.headline: New car sales drop for eighth consecutive month as one million buyers exit market
cards.body:
New car sales in the United States have declined for the eighth straight month, with one million buyers who previously purchased new vehicles no longer doing so, according to industry data. The sustained sales slump reflects mounting financial pressure on American drivers.

The Wall Street Journal reported that these one million buyers are gone and not expected to return soon. Auto sales have crashed across the board, with electric vehicle demand experiencing a particularly steep collapse as drivers face economic constraints.

Despite the sales downturn, automakers continue to generate profits, according to a NewsNation report. The industry has managed to maintain profitability even as fewer Americans can afford new vehicles, suggesting pricing strategies have compensated for lower sales volumes.

USA Today examined why over one million drivers are declining to purchase new cars. The trend has transformed new car ownership from a routine purchase into an increasingly distant prospect for many American households.

The sustained nature of the decline marks a significant shift in the automotive market. Eight consecutive months of falling sales represents the longest downturn in recent years, indicating structural changes in consumer purchasing power rather than temporary market fluctuations.

Yahoo Finance attributed the collapse partly to weakening demand for electric vehicles specifically, though the sales decline extends across all vehicle categories. The dual pressure of high vehicle prices and broader economic squeeze has left many potential buyers unable to justify new car purchases.

Industry analysts tracking the trend note that the missing one million buyers represent a substantial portion of the new car market. Their absence has reshaped dealer inventories and manufacturer production planning, though companies have adjusted pricing to preserve margins on remaining sales.

cards.headline: Green card applicants face new Trump administration requirements
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has begun implementing new green card policies, creating confusion about whether applicants must leave the country.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has started making new requests of green card applicants, leading to widespread confusion and anxiety among immigrants. Initial messaging from the administration suggested many applicants would need to leave the United States to obtain permanent residency.

The Department of Homeland Security later clarified that most immigrants would not need to depart the country to receive green cards. The conflicting messages prompted concern among immigration advocates and applicants about what the policy changes actually require.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo Kills More Than 245
cards.body:
A severe Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed at least 65 confirmed deaths, with health officials reporting 246 suspected cases in Ituri province. The World Health Organization estimates the death rate between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases, describing it as extremely high.

The outbreak is concentrated in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with additional suspected cases reported in the neighboring city of Bunia. Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan, has become the center of the crisis. The region's status as a hub for mining towns creates particular challenges, as constant movement of people through these areas complicates disease control efforts.

The strain identified in the outbreak is Bundibugyo Ebola, which differs from the more commonly seen Zaire strain. Critically, no licensed vaccine currently exists for Bundibugyo, though vaccines are available for other Ebola types. The Africa Centres for Disease Control detected the virus in 13 of 20 samples tested by the DRC's national research laboratory.

Uganda has already confirmed cases within its borders. A 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC, marking the disease's spread across international boundaries. Officials at the Africa CDC have expressed serious concern about further regional transmission given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières has described the virus spread as deeply alarming. Health workers in the region face significant obstacles, including limited equipment and resources as they attempt to contain the outbreak. The WHO chief visited the most affected areas to support containment efforts.

Ebola is a severe viral illness spread through direct contact with body fluids, including blood and vomit from infected people, as well as contact with dead bodies during funeral preparations. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, and bleeding.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. Experts point to multiple factors contributing to these recurring crises. Close contact between humans and animal reservoirs, likely bats or primates, creates transmission opportunities. Additional risk factors include movement between rural and urban areas, tropical climate conditions, and extensive rainforest coverage.

The Africa CDC has convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, the World Health Organization, and pharmaceutical companies to coordinate response efforts. The outbreak represents a major public health crisis requiring sustained international coordination and resources to prevent further spread across the region and beyond.

cards.headline: Colombian Presidential Election Set for Sunday
cards.teaser: A leftist candidate leads in polls ahead of Colombia's presidential vote, while a far-right rival has gained momentum.
cards.body:
Colombia holds presidential elections on Sunday with a leftist candidate leading in polls, though facing competition from a far-right challenger.

Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa has been accused of interfering in the election after offering to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing presidential candidate. The tariff offer came just before the vote, raising concerns about foreign meddling in Colombia's electoral process.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers, marking a major commitment to European computing infrastructure. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The investment reflects surging demand for data infrastructure as artificial intelligence and cloud services continue to expand globally.

cards.headline: Drone Strike Hits Apartment Building in Eastern Romania
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war close to home for residents.
cards.body:
A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, causing a fire and panic among residents. The crash served as a reminder to people living in the area that the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war poses dangers to neighboring countries.

Residents described hearing a big bang before the fire broke out. People who had evacuated began returning to check on their homes in the affected building. Many said they no longer feel safe following the strike.

cards.headline: Colombian Presidential Election Set for Sunday
cards.teaser: A leftist candidate leads in polls ahead of Colombia's presidential vote, while a far-right rival has gained momentum.
cards.body:
Colombia holds presidential elections on Sunday with a leftist candidate leading in polls, though facing competition from a far-right challenger.

Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa has been accused of interfering in the election after offering to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing presidential candidate. The tariff offer came just before the vote, raising concerns about foreign meddling in Colombia's electoral process.

cards.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
cards.teaser: The film editor, who was the ex-wife of director George Lucas, was recognized as a pivotal creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy.
cards.body:
Marcia Lucas, the acclaimed film editor behind the original Star Wars trilogy, has died at age 80. She was recognized as a crucial creative force in shaping the groundbreaking space films.

Lucas, the ex-wife of director George Lucas, earned an Oscar for her editing work on the trilogy. Her contributions were essential to the films' success and their profound cultural impact on cinema.

cards.headline: Australian Farmers Face Mouse Plague Destroying Crops
cards.teaser: Farmers report thousands of mice per hectare are destroying crops and invading homes across Australia.
cards.body:
Australian farmers are battling a mouse plague that is destroying crops and invading homes. Farmers report finding thousands of mice per hectare in affected areas.

One farmer described the situation as resembling a decaying body. The rodents are causing widespread damage to agricultural operations and forcing their way into residential buildings.

cards.headline: Iranian Soccer Team Practicing in Turkey While Awaiting US Visas
cards.teaser: Iranian soccer players are training in Turkey and making backup plans as they wait for visas to enter the United States for the World Cup.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team is training in Turkey while waiting for visas to enter the United States. The players are preparing for the World Cup, which is overshadowed by ongoing tensions.

The team is practicing in limbo and developing backup plans in case the visas are not approved in time. The situation reflects the broader geopolitical complications affecting international sporting events.

cards.headline: Concerts by Ye and Travis Scott Canceled in Italy
cards.teaser: Italian authorities canceled concerts by Ye and Travis Scott over security concerns and objections from Jewish leaders.
cards.body:
Kanye West, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, was set to perform at the Pulse of Gaia festival at RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia on July 18. However, the city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, canceled the concert citing "public order and safety issues."

The cancellation followed concerns raised by the local Jewish community about West's previous antisemitic remarks. Authorities determined that the performance posed risks to public safety that could not be mitigated.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump's Kennedy Center renaming and closure
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled against Trump's plan to rename and potentially close the Kennedy Center, prompting an angry response from the president.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's attempt to rename and close the Kennedy Center, a performing arts venue in Washington. The ruling prevents Trump from implementing changes to the facility that bears the Kennedy name.

Trump responded to the decision by attacking the judge's wife following the court order.

cards.headline: Hunger strike at New Jersey immigration facility reaches ninth day
cards.teaser: Protesters and Trump supporters faced off outside a New Jersey ICE detention center as a hunger strike by detainees entered its ninth day.
cards.body:
A hunger and labor strike at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey reached its ninth day on Saturday. Detained immigrants are demanding improved conditions and medical care.

Competing demonstrations unfolded outside the facility as supporters of the detained immigrants and Trump-supporting counterprotesters gathered behind barricades set up by state police. The groups exchanged chants and slogans across the dividing line.

cards.headline: Green card applicants face new Trump administration requirements
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has begun implementing new green card policies, creating confusion about whether applicants must leave the country.

The Trump administration has started making new requests of green card applicants, leading to widespread confusion and anxiety among immigrants. Initial messaging from the administration suggested many applicants would need to leave the United States to obtain permanent residency.

The Department of Homeland Security later clarified that most immigrants would not need to depart the country to receive green cards. The conflicting messages prompted concern among immigration advocates and applicants about what the policy changes actually require.

cards.headline: Catholic priest convicted of sexually assaulting women in Texas
cards.teaser: Father Anthony Odiong was found guilty on all counts of sexually abusing women who were under his spiritual care.
cards.body:
A jury in Texas convicted Father Anthony Odiong of sexually assaulting women he counseled as a Catholic priest. The verdict found him guilty on all counts in the trial, which centered on allegations that he abused his position of spiritual authority.

A Louisiana chapel that Odiong built has removed his name from the facility following the conviction. The case has raised questions about several Church leaders and their oversight. Prosecutors described faith as the weapon Odiong used to exploit the women who trusted him for spiritual guidance.

cards.headline: Longview mill disaster leaves community seeking answers
cards.teaser: A tank implosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, killed and injured workers, with survivors facing long recoveries from severe burns.
cards.body:
An explosion at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington, caused deaths and serious injuries to workers. Survivors of the tank implosion are facing extended recovery periods after suffering severe burns from white liquor, a chemical used in paper production.

The community has raised thousands of dollars for families affected by the disaster. One family described trying every way to contact their loved one after the incident. Investigators have said something went dramatically wrong at the facility, but few answers have emerged about what caused the explosion.

cards.headline: Meteor explosion causes loud boom across New England
cards.teaser: A meteorologist confirmed that a meteor exploded off the Massachusetts coast, creating a sonic boom heard by hundreds across the region.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded in the atmosphere off the coast of Massachusetts, producing a sonic boom that reverberated across Southern New England. The mid-air explosion was heard and felt by hundreds of residents throughout the region, initially causing confusion about its source.

Meteorologists confirmed the meteor as the cause of the loud noise, resolving questions from residents who reported the boom.

cards.headline: United flight diverted to Wisconsin after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison after a 75-year-old passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. The 75-year-old man was restrained by crew members and other passengers during the incident.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison, where authorities took the passenger into custody. Local officials indicated they do not expect to file charges.

cards.headline: Blue Origin faces months of delays following rocket explosion that damaged launch pad
cards.teaser: An explosion involving a Blue Origin rocket has damaged the company's launch pad, forcing delays of several months to its launch schedule.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a test. The blast caused significant damage to the facility, forcing the company to suspend operations while repairs are completed.

The incident will set back Blue Origin's launch schedule by several months as the company rebuilds the necessary infrastructure. This explosion marks a major setback for the aerospace company's efforts to establish operational launch capabilities.

cards.headline: China's drug development industry draws scrutiny at international oncology conference
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are receiving attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China have become a focus of discussion at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The attention underscores China's rapidly expanding biotechnology sector and its growing involvement in drug development worldwide.

The surge in Chinese biotechnology capabilities has prompted concerns in the United States about declining American dominance in pharmaceuticals. Industry observers are closely monitoring China's expanding role in clinical research and drug development.

cards.headline: High IPO valuations for SpaceX and AI companies signal poor outlook for retail investors
cards.teaser: When newly public companies receive valuations as high as those anticipated for SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic, ordinary investors have historically faced poor returns.
cards.body:
Companies valued at the levels expected for upcoming initial public offerings from SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic have historically delivered weak performance for ordinary investors. The sky-high pricing at which these firms are likely to go public reduces the potential for retail shareholders to see gains.

One analyst issued a recommendation that investors avoid the SpaceX IPO entirely. The Verge reported that the offering is positioned to benefit Elon Musk while providing limited upside for regular investors who buy shares at the inflated public market price.

cards.headline: C.H. Robinson removes carriers based on safety scores following Supreme Court ruling
cards.teaser: The logistics company has begun removing carriers from its network based on safety performance, a move that may be connected to a recent Supreme Court decision affecting broker liability.
cards.body:
C.H. Robinson has begun removing carriers from its network based on safety scores, following a Supreme Court ruling issued two weeks prior. The court decision addressed broker immunity and liability issues in the transportation industry.

Legal observers have characterized the ruling as significant for trucking safety, suggesting it may create stronger incentives for brokers to more carefully evaluate carrier safety records. This development indicates the decision could reshape how freight brokers approach carrier selection and oversight.

cards.headline: Schneider Electric uses AI to boost worker productivity instead of cutting jobs
cards.teaser: The French multinational deployed artificial intelligence in its manufacturing operations to enhance worker output rather than replace employees.
cards.body:
Schneider Electric, a French multinational corporation, implemented artificial intelligence technology in its manufacturing facilities with the goal of making workers more productive rather than eliminating positions. The approach represents an alternative to the typical deployment of automation to reduce headcount.

The company's strategy focused on using AI as a tool to augment human capabilities rather than substitute for them. By prioritizing productivity gains over workforce reduction, Schneider Electric pursued a different path than many manufacturers adopting similar technologies.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher over zero-day exploit disclosures
hero.body:
Microsoft has threatened legal action against a security researcher for publicly disclosing multiple zero-day vulnerabilities without first coordinating with the company, reigniting a longstanding debate over software security practices.

The researcher, who goes by Nightmare-Eclipse, published six zero-day exploits publicly. Microsoft responded by condemning what it called uncoordinated disclosures and warning of potential criminal investigation. The company has since involved law enforcement in the matter.

Zero-day vulnerabilities are software flaws unknown to vendors, making them especially dangerous since no patches exist when discovered. Industry standard practice calls for coordinated disclosure, where researchers privately notify companies of vulnerabilities and allow time for patch development before public release.

Microsoft's decision to escalate beyond typical responses has drawn criticism from portions of the cybersecurity community. Security researchers have described the situation as humiliating for Nightmare-Eclipse. In response to Microsoft's legal threats, the researcher pledged what they called a "bone shattering drop," suggesting additional vulnerability information may be released, though specifics remain unclear.

Some posts from Nightmare-Eclipse suggest they may be a disgruntled former Microsoft employee. Their public confrontation with the company highlights ongoing tension between security researchers and software vendors. Researchers sometimes argue that public disclosure pressures companies to fix problems faster, while vendors maintain that private reporting protects users by preventing exploitation during patch development.

Microsoft has not publicly specified what legal violations it believes occurred. The company's involvement of law enforcement represents a significant escalation beyond cease-and-desist letters or public statements typically used in disclosure disputes.

The six zero-day vulnerabilities affect Microsoft products, though specific details about which software was impacted and the severity of the flaws have not been disclosed. Whether Microsoft has since patched any of the disclosed vulnerabilities remains unclear.

Kevin Beaumont, a cybersecurity researcher, flagged the situation as particularly notable for how Microsoft handled the disclosure dispute. The case underscores fundamental disagreements within the technology sector about responsible vulnerability handling.

This dispute comes amid broader debates about cybersecurity responsibility. The tension between independent researchers and major software companies reflects competing priorities: vendors prioritize controlled patching processes while researchers sometimes believe public pressure accelerates fixes and protects users by raising visibility around threats.

Microsoft's approach differs markedly from how the industry typically handles these conflicts. Most companies work to resolve disclosure disputes through negotiation or legal channels without involving law enforcement, making Microsoft's decision to call authorities a notable departure from standard practice.

The outcome of this dispute could influence how technology companies respond to future uncoordinated disclosures and may reshape the relationship between independent security researchers and major vendors.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers, marking a major commitment to European computing infrastructure. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The investment reflects surging demand for data infrastructure as artificial intelligence and cloud services continue to expand globally.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemini Spark AI assistant to Ultra subscribers
cards.teaser: The new feature automates everyday tasks including inbox summaries and local event planning, though it exists as a separate product from the main Gemini service.
cards.body:
Google rolled out Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI assistant, to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the United States. The tool automates everyday digital tasks, including summarizing inbox messages and planning local events while running continuously in the background.

Reviewers found the assistant genuinely useful for handling routine chores. However, questions have emerged about Google's decision to launch Spark as a separate product rather than integrating these capabilities directly into the existing Gemini assistant.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing, drawing developer criticism
cards.teaser: Microsoft's coding assistant moved away from its previous pricing model, prompting complaints from software developers.
cards.body:
GitHub Copilot introduced a new token-based billing system, replacing its previous pricing structure. The change has generated complaints among developers who use the AI coding assistant.

Developers criticized the new payment model, with some suggesting the shift marks the end of what they considered a golden age for the product. Token-based billing charges users based on the amount of AI-generated code they consume rather than a flat subscription fee.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: Twenty alumni from the social media company created a new fund to back the next generation of social platforms.
cards.body:
Twenty Snap alumni have joined forces to establish Ghost Angels, an investment fund dedicated to backing emerging social media startups. The group aims to support the next generation of social platforms as they develop.

The fund's name draws from Snap's iconic ghost mascot, reflecting both the founders' heritage at the company and their new role as investors in the social media space.

cards.headline: Meta developing AI pendant hardware
cards.teaser: The social media company is working on wearable AI technology as it expands its hardware ambitions.
cards.body:
Meta is developing an AI-powered pendant, according to reports. The device would represent another piece of artificial intelligence hardware from the company.

The pendant project suggests Meta is making significant investments in AI-powered hardware beyond its existing virtual reality headsets and smart glasses. The company has not publicly announced the product or disclosed its planned features.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases new backwards compatibility updates for Switch 2
cards.teaser: The gaming company issued fixes allowing more original Switch games to run on its newer console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released a new wave of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on Switch 2. The updates address issues preventing some original Switch titles from working properly on the newer hardware.

The patches continue Nintendo's efforts to ensure its library of Switch games remains playable on the Switch 2 console. Backwards compatibility has been a priority for the company as it transitions users to new hardware.

hero.headline: PSG wins second consecutive Champions League title on penalties against Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain successfully defended their Champions League crown by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout at the final in Budapest. The victory marks the French club's second consecutive European championship.

The match remained locked at 1-1 after 90 minutes and extra time. Arsenal striker Kai Havertz gave the English club an early lead, while PSG equalized through Ousmane Dembélé from the penalty spot in the second half. The shootout ultimately decided the winner, with Gabriel Magalhães missing the decisive penalty for Arsenal as his shot sailed over the crossbar.

Arsenal reached the final seeking their first-ever Champions League title. The club had previously appeared in a European Cup final only once before, in 2006, when Barcelona defeated them. This season represented a historic campaign for Arsenal, who clinched their first Premier League title in 22 years before traveling to Budapest for the continental showdown.

Manager Mikel Arteta expressed disappointment after the loss but emphasized the need to learn from the experience. He stated his team would need to improve to achieve a different outcome in future competitions. Arteta highlighted a controversial decision during the match, noting that Arsenal should have received a penalty late in the first half of extra time.

Despite the loss, Arsenal's campaign demonstrated significant progress. The club competed throughout the tournament and performed strongly in the first half, frustrating PSG with defensive organization and tactical discipline. Bukayo Saka, Arsenal's England forward who had scored in last season's semi-final defeat against PSG, expressed that reaching the final represented another exciting opportunity to create history for the club.

Arteta had entered the final with confidence in his players' ability to win. Before the match, he discussed the hunger within the squad following their Premier League success, noting that the team wanted additional trophies and possessed the capability to achieve them.

PSG completed an impressive knockout stage run, eliminating Chelsea, Liverpool, and Bayern Munich en route to the final. The French club's back-to-back titles place them among Europe's most successful teams in the modern era and cement their position as continental football's dominant force.

Arsenal's season concluded with 63 matches played, more than any other team from Europe's top five leagues. Saka had predicted that fatigue would not determine the outcome, arguing instead that quality moments and organization would prove decisive. However, the penalty shootout proved to be Arsenal's undoing.

The defeat represents another near-miss for Arsenal, who finished second in the Premier League title race three consecutive seasons before finally capturing the domestic crown this year. Arteta's challenge now involves channeling the disappointment from the Champions League loss into motivation for continued success.

cards.headline: Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open in third round
cards.teaser: The defending champion lost to Anastasia Potapova, ending her title defense.
cards.body:
Defending champion Coco Gauff has been eliminated from the French Open in the third round, losing to No. 28 seed Anastasia Potapova 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4. Potapova recovered from a set down to claim the upset victory in a tightly contested match.

Gauff, seeded fourth, had led by a break in the final set but faltered down the stretch, losing five of the last six games. The American acknowledged missing crucial opportunities under pressure, citing missed backhands at key moments when she held break points at 3-all in the decisive set.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Gilmour sustained the injury during a friendly match against Curacao.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury during Saturday's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao.

Despite the decisive win, Scotland's preparations for their first World Cup appearance in 28 years have been dampened by Gilmour's absence. Manager Steve Clarke will need to find a replacement for the injured midfielder ahead of Scotland's opening match against Haiti. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential option to fill the gap in the squad.

cards.headline: Vegas Golden Knights and Carolina Hurricanes to meet in Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The NHL announced ticket sale details for the championship series.
cards.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes have reached the Stanley Cup Final for the first time in 20 years, breaking through their Eastern Conference barrier after eight years of playoff heartbreak. Head coach Rod Brind'Amour led the team to victory over Montreal, securing the Prince of Wales Trophy.

The Golden Knights will face Carolina in a matchup between two nontraditional hockey markets. The Hurricanes will host Games 1 and 2 of the championship series, with additional contests taking place in Las Vegas. Ticket sale information for the Finals has been announced.

cards.headline: Adam Azim stops Steve Claggett in third round in London
cards.teaser: The British light-welterweight moved closer to a world title shot with the victory.
cards.body:
British light-welterweight Adam Azim defeated Steve Claggett with a third-round stoppage in London. The win advances Azim's pursuit of a world title opportunity.

Azim controlled the fight before securing the stoppage victory early in the bout. The performance demonstrated his readiness for higher-level competition in the division.

cards.headline: Newcastle completes record comeback to defeat Sale Sharks
cards.teaser: The win came on the final play of the match and damages Sale's Champions Cup hopes.
cards.body:
Newcastle staged an incredible comeback to stun Sale Sharks, securing victory with the final play of the game. The win represents a record-breaking comeback in the competition's history.

The defeat dealt a significant blow to Sale's hopes of qualifying for the Champions Cup, while Newcastle claimed two crucial points in their push up the standings.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball faces Texas Tech in Women's College World Series
cards.teaser: The teams met in a winners' bracket game at the NCAA tournament.
cards.body:
Number 7 Tennessee played number 11 Texas Tech in a Women's College World Series winners' bracket matchup. The game followed both teams advancing through earlier rounds of the NCAA softball tournament.

Tennessee pitcher Karlyn Pickens started for the Lady Vols in the tournament game. The winner advanced further in the double-elimination bracket while the loser dropped to the elimination side.

hero.headline: Oscar-winning Star Wars editor Marcia Lucas dies at 80
hero.body:
Lucas won the Academy Award for Best Film Editing for her work on the first Star Wars film in 1977. She also edited American Graffiti and worked on The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. Her contributions to the original Star Wars included shaping the final space battle and reshaping the overall structure of the film.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas worked on several other notable films during the 1970s and early 1980s. She was married to Star Wars creator George Lucas from 1969 to 1983. After their divorce, she largely stepped away from the film industry.

Her editing work on Star Wars proved transformative for the final product. She was among the editors who restructured the film during post-production, helping turn what had been a challenging production into a cultural phenomenon. The film went on to become one of the highest-grossing movies of all time and launched a franchise that continues today.

Lucas was born in 1945. She began her career in the film industry working as an assistant editor before moving into lead editing roles. Her partnership with George Lucas on American Graffiti in 1973 helped establish both of their careers in Hollywood.

Her work on the original Star Wars trilogy remains influential in film editing. She was part of a team that pioneered techniques for editing science fiction action sequences that became standard practice in the industry. The Academy Award she received recognized her technical skill and creative contribution to cinema.

After stepping away from Hollywood, Lucas maintained a low public profile. She gave occasional interviews about her work on Star Wars and other films but largely stayed out of the spotlight.

The film industry has acknowledged her contributions to the Star Wars franchise and to editing as a craft. Her death marks the loss of one of the key creative figures behind the original trilogy.

cards.headline: Italy cancels Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts over security concerns
cards.teaser: Authorities in Italy have banned scheduled concerts by rappers Kanye West and Travis Scott citing public order and safety issues.
cards.body:
Kanye West's scheduled performance at the Pulse of Gaia festival in Reggio Emilia, Italy on July 18 has been cancelled by the city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri. The decision followed concerns raised by the local Jewish community regarding West's previous antisemitic remarks.

Authorities cited "public order and safety issues" as the reason for stopping the concert. West, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, was set to perform at the RCF Arena in the northern Italian city.

cards.headline: Hannah Waddingham says she never auditioned for Wicked role
cards.teaser: The Ted Lasso actor addressed speculation about trying out for the role of Madame Morrible in the Wicked film adaptation.
cards.body:
Hannah Waddingham confirmed she never auditioned for the role of Madame Morrible in the film adaptation of Wicked. The actor addressed speculation that had circulated about her involvement with the musical film project.

Waddingham shut down claims regarding a failed audition for the part. The role of Madame Morrible in Wicked has been the subject of casting discussion, but Waddingham clarified she was not among those who tried out for it.

cards.headline: Pete Davidson praises ex-girlfriend Kim Kardashian in podcast appearance
cards.teaser: The comedian called Kardashian superhuman and complimented her acting skills during an interview with Nikki Glaser.
cards.body:
Pete Davidson spoke positively about his ex-girlfriend Kim Kardashian during a podcast with Nikki Glaser. The comedian described Kardashian as superhuman and praised her acting abilities, saying she is good at performing.

Davidson and Kardashian dated before splitting almost four years ago. His comments represent rare public remarks about his former relationship with the reality television star and businesswoman. Davidson made the statements while appearing as a guest on the podcast.

cards.headline: Trump suggests he might headline freedom concerts after artists drop out
cards.teaser: Multiple music acts have canceled performances at a Trump-backed concert series for America's 250th anniversary celebration.
cards.body:
Donald Trump said he may perform at his own event after several musicians withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series tied to America's 250th birthday celebration. Performers including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride cited concerns that the event would become political.

Trump announced plans to hold an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday to replace the concert series. The former president is also set to headline the Great American State Fair following the artists' departures.

cards.headline: Tom Holland says he wants to help set up next Spider-Man star
cards.teaser: The actor told Empire magazine he would like to mentor whoever takes over the Marvel franchise role.
cards.body:
Tom Holland told Empire magazine he looks forward to eventually passing the Spider-Man role to the next actor. He expressed interest in mentoring whoever takes on the character next, whether that's Miles Morales or another version of Spider-Man.

Holland drew inspiration from Robert Downey Jr., who mentored him when he joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He hopes to provide similar guidance to establish the next chapter for a new Spider-Man star.

cards.headline: Kirk Cameron says he left California for Tennessee over politics
cards.teaser: The Growing Pains actor explained his move on the Adam Carolla Podcast, citing concerns about raising a family.
cards.body:
Kirk Cameron said he moved from California to Tennessee to escape what he called the state's terrible politics and other factors that make it difficult to raise a family. The former Growing Pains star made the comments during an appearance on the Adam Carolla Podcast.

Cameron told the podcast that California is great when you are a child because your parents pay for everything. He left the Golden State for Tennessee, where he now lives.

hero.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
hero.body:
U.S. Central Command announced on Saturday that it prevented another vessel from docking at an Iranian port as part of its ongoing naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The military disabled a ship flying under a Gambian flag on Friday after the vessel ignored repeated warnings, according to a Centcom statement. The action represents the latest enforcement of restrictions the U.S. has placed on Iranian ports and the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical shipping channel for global oil supplies. The U.S. blockade reflects the strategic importance of the waterway to international commerce and energy markets.

Centcom did not provide specific details about the extent of damage to the disabled vessel or information about the condition of its crew. The military statement only confirmed that the ship failed to comply with warnings before U.S. forces took action.

The incident occurs amid a broader confrontation in the region with multiple environmental consequences. The U.S. has sunk several Iranian vessels at the start of military operations, while Iran has used drones and missiles to strike container ships and oil tankers in an effort to police its own blockade of the strait.

One significant casualty has been the Shahid Bagheri, an Iranian Navy vessel described as a converted container ship equipped with a short runway for launching drones. The ship was struck by U.S. warplanes on March 6 and subsequently grounded in shallow waters in the Khuran strait. The vessel has been leaking heavy fuel oil in Iranian territorial waters, creating an environmental hazard.

Satellite analysis indicates the oil slick has traveled westward toward the Hara biosphere reserve, the largest mangrove forest on the Gulf shoreline. As of March 18, the oil had moved approximately 16 miles southwest toward the ecologically sensitive area. Rainfall on March 27 appeared to accelerate the spill's movement further.

The potential impact on the Hara region could be significant. The area serves as critical habitat for migrating birds, critically endangered turtles, and numerous species of fish and crustaceans. Coastal fishing communities in the region depend almost entirely on the sea for their livelihoods.

The environmental damage extends beyond this single spill. Multiple incidents have occurred in the Gulf, including three small spills off the coasts of Iraq and Kuwait and another in the strait from a sunken container ship. A U.S. torpedo attack on the Iranian navy ship Dena off Sri Lanka also caused a spill that was handled by Sri Lankan authorities.

Environmental analysts warn the situation could deteriorate. With ongoing military strikes targeting ships in the region, the risk of more significant environmental disasters remains high.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to examine a controversial fund that has divided Republicans since its announcement earlier this month.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which was settled through an $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund announced in May. The case stems from the leak of Trump's and his sons' personal and business tax returns by a former contractor.

Miami Judge Kathleen Williams agreed to revisit the settlement after a third-party motion claimed the agreement is a "product of collusion and itself a fraud on the court." The fund has drawn significant backlash since its announcement, revealing divisions within the Republican Party over its legitimacy and purpose.

cards.headline: Trump calls court system rigged after recent rulings
cards.teaser: The president criticized the judiciary following decisions blocking tariff policy and the Kennedy Center renaming.
cards.body:
President Trump called the U.S. court system "rigged" on Saturday following recent judicial decisions that blocked key elements of his administration's agenda. The rulings blocked a cornerstone of his economic policy and prevented the addition of his name to the Kennedy Center.

Trump's criticism reflects frustration with multiple setbacks to his priorities across both economic and cultural initiatives.

cards.headline: Senate candidate's wife reported sexual messages to campaign staff
cards.teaser: Graham Platner's wife told senior campaign aides he had exchanged explicit messages with other women.
cards.body:
Amy Gertner, wife of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner, informed campaign staff last year that her husband had exchanged sexually explicit messages with other women. The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal reported that Gertner told former senior campaign staffer Genevieve McDonald about the messages.

Platner is seeking the Democratic nomination for Senate in Maine. The reports surfaced as his campaign continues ahead of upcoming primary elections.

cards.headline: Trump plans rally after artists withdraw from America 250 celebration
cards.teaser: The president announced a political rally after several performers canceled appearances at the National Mall event.
cards.body:
President Trump announced plans to hold an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday to replace a concert series for the nation's 250th anniversary celebration. The decision came after several performers, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride, withdrew from the event citing concerns that it would become political.

Trump made the announcement during a Saturday posting spree on Truth Social, in which he posted 25 times within two hours while at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia. He dismissed the artists' departure, suggesting they were experiencing performance anxiety about the event.

cards.headline: White House denies report on Vance social media advice
cards.teaser: Administration officials rejected a New York Times story about the chief of staff advising the vice president.
cards.body:
The White House denied a New York Times report claiming chief of staff Susie Wiles advised Vice President Vance to take a break from social media. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung dismissed the story as "complete fake news" in a post on X.

Cheung's denial came shortly after the Times published the report. The administration did not provide additional details about the alleged advice or Vance's social media usage.

cards.headline: Security preparations underway for America 250 events in Washington
cards.teaser: The capital is preparing for anniversary celebrations amid concerns about political violence.
cards.body:
Security measures are being implemented across Washington ahead of celebrations for the nation's 250th anniversary this summer. The first event, a UFC fight at the White House, will take place in the coming weeks.

The preparations follow a shooting outside the White House complex and come two months after another security incident. Multiple events are planned throughout the summer to mark the anniversary.
